newsitem.title: THAILAND: Review of BBC takeover bids completed.
newsitem.headline: Review of BBC takeover bids completed.

text.p: A preliminary review by the government of bids for Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) has been completed and its result will be passed on Wednesday to the troubled bank's controlling panel, a senior finance ministry official said on Tuesday.
Vuthichai Pongprasit, deputy permanent secretary for finance and a member of the bids review committee, declined to give details of offers made by three private groups seeking to take over BBC.
BBC has been placed under government control since May when central bank officials said the bank was saddled with over 70 billion baht ($2.8 billion) of risky and non-performing loans.
Private consortia bidding for BBC are groups represented by Nithipat Capital Plc, SITCA Investment and Securities Plc, and Black Forrest Holding Corp.

BBC executives said the Nithipat-led group had proposed complicated conditions to take over BBC while SITCA put in a more straightforward offer after its recent application for a commercial bank licence was rejected by the government.

Assistant central bank governor Chusri Daengprapai described Black Forrest's bid as the most impressive on paper but she said the authorities would like more information on the sources of its takeover funds.

BBC sources said Nithipat and SITCA had offered to buy 30 percent of BBC's 35 million shares at a 10-baht par price on condition that the bank's risky and non-performing loans be first transferred to a subsidiary of the central bank's Financial Institutions Rehabilitation Fund.

The sources said Black Forrest had proposed to buy 40 percent of BBC's shares at 20 baht each before making a cash injection into the bank within a month. The group said it planned to set up a separate company to handle the bank's doubtful debts.
Black Forrest, incorporated in Thailand with a 10 million baht capital, is headed by American major shareholders Saul Rottenbach and John Wagner.
